Print to “InkPrint EPUB” to get a reflowable e-book instead of a PDF. Text, headings and pictures are rebuilt on this device; tables are kept as pictures.

Off: scanned pages stay pictures — faster

Add the recognised text, invisibly, to scanned pages: select, copy, search and look up words, with the page unchanged

InkPrint is open source.

Suggestions or problems? Write to:
%1$s

Thank you for your support!
Add “InkPrint” on the computer or phone you print from.
There are two printers: “InkPrint” saves a PDF, “InkPrint EPUB” saves a reflowable e-book. Add one or both.
Manual — Terminal (by IP, e.g. over Tailscale / VPN)
Always choose the driverless option (AirPrint, IPP Everywhere, IPP Class Driver) — InkPrint only accepts PDF.
Auto-discovery only works on the same Wi-Fi. Over Tailscale / VPN, use the manual steps with this device’s VPN address.
Apple menu → System Settings → Printers & Scanners
InkPrint and InkPrint EPUB are listed — select one
“Use: AirPrint” is selected automatically → click Add
To add the other printer too, repeat steps 2–4
Don’t add it as “Generic PostScript Printer”: that sends PostScript, and InkPrint only accepts PDF.
Click “Add device” — InkPrint appears on the same network
Click “Add device” — InkPrint and InkPrint EPUB appear on the same network
Click “Add device” next to the one you want (or both)
If it doesn’t show up, add it by IP address:
Add device → “The printer that I want isn’t listed”
Select “Add a printer using an IP address or hostname”
Device type: IPP Device. Hostname or IP address:
Driver: Microsoft IPP Class Driver, then Next to finish
For the EPUB printer, repeat with queue ipp/epub and name it InkPrint EPUB
Don’t pick “Generic / Text Only” or a PostScript driver: they don’t send PDF, and the job is rejected.
Works on Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch and most distributions.
Don’t pick a Generic, PostScript or vendor driver: those don’t send PDF.
iPhone and iPad print with AirPrint out of the box.
Start the InkPrint service on the reader
Connect the iPhone / iPad to the same Wi-Fi
Tap “Printer” — InkPrint and InkPrint EPUB appear automatically
Tap Print — the PDF is saved on the reader
Tap Print — InkPrint saves a PDF, InkPrint EPUB an e-book
A reader connected to the iPhone’s own hotspot can’t be discovered. Use a shared Wi-Fi router.
Start InkPrint on the reader, on the same Wi-Fi
Settings → Connected devices → Connection preferences → Printing
InkPrint and InkPrint EPUB appear automatically
In any app, Share / Print → InkPrint
In any app, Share / Print → InkPrint or InkPrint EPUB
In Default Print Service, tap ⋮ → Add printer
Add printer by IP address, with the port:
Adding by IP only reaches the PDF printer — Android can’t take a printer path. Use auto-discovery for InkPrint EPUB.
